Parallel sentence corpus

Romanized Qaroshi → native glyphs

Each handwritten glyph is retained from the supplied 26-letter alphabet. The four digraphs sh zh kh ng are each a single letter. Typographic punctuation and Arabic digits are additional technical marks, not native glyphs.

The original alphabet is artwork, not a keyboard-installable font. This converter renders that artwork directly. The dictionary searches words but does not automatically translate unrestricted English.

Core grammar reference

A full sentence begins with exactly one written resonance marker and follows a predominantly subject–object–verb pattern. A clause's finite verb comes after its main arguments, and negation nu directly precedes its predicate.

mëaffection, vulnerability

qorsolemnity, promises
senneutral information
hëinquiry
lënshyness

Word order and endings

REGISTER + subject + object-m + place/time + nu? + verb + evidence? + he?/ya?. Nouns: -ri plural, -na possession, -lo location, -gu goal, -de source, -wa with, -tu recipient, -shi instrument, -nga via/through. Verbs: -te past, -yu future, -se ongoing, -mo complete, -në habitual; -ki can, -ho allowed, -du must.

Advanced structures

wë if, wënu counterfactual if, qinë would (consequent), yëmë optative wish, dasha even if, shoru unless, qona embedded whether, rëshi contrastive focus, toru quotation introducer, hëmi confirmation tag.

Questions use final he (except confirmation questions with hëmi); requests use ya. Evidentials: si witnessed, hu reported, ye inferred, lëshu customary knowledge. The traditional number system is base six.

3.0 discourse and timing

Preverbal phase: wëshi about to, shëtë just finished, zhoro still, mënoro nu not yet, nësha nu no longer. Focus: ngëshi only, bëso also, tëmiri even. Quantity: noun + qësho / rëshu / nëmi + numeral. Evidence: shëku remembered, wërusha measured, rëhu written source; yëqo surprising result, sëki / qëru low/high confidence. See docs/grammar_v3_extensions.md in the ZIP for full precedence rules and more examples.

For the formal details and exceptions see docs/grammar.md in the complete reference pack.

Qaroshi Reference 3.0. Lexical coverage remains a milestone toward full modern-language expressiveness, not a claim of idiomatic parity. All content is bundled in this file. Original alphabet artwork retained.
